1.pericope_label: The word that came to Jeremiah after that Nebuzaradan had let him go from Ramah
debates: What the opening title belongs to
Whether the prophet was bound by accident or by design
How much the confession of the captain of the guard means
outliers: Calvin holds the prophet was brought out in chains deliberately, to expose the ingratitude of the nation
Ellicott limits the confession of the Chaldean general to the ordinary belief that each nation has its own guardian deity
themes: A heading with no prophecy under it
A prophet bound among those he had warned
Sentence pronounced from the bench instead of the pulpit
Liberty offered where captivity was expected

5.pericope_label: Go back also to Gedaliah, and dwell with him among the people
debates: Whose words the opening clause is
Whether it would have gone better with the prophet had he left
outliers: Ellicott reads the title given to Gedaliah as evidence that the capital was treated as blotted out and needing no superintendence
Calvin holds that the prophet remaining in the land was itself a standard raised to invite the captives back
themes: A discharge amended on second thoughts
Office under a conqueror defended as patriotism
A refusal that might have given offence
A site disputed between two ridges

7.pericope_label: When all the captains of the forces heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor
debates: Where the captains had been during the siege
Where the places named in the list lay
Whether the parallel list gives the same names
outliers: Calvin rejects the common view that the captains fled with the king when the city fell, since the king and his companions were all overtaken together
Henry observes that the prophet had nowhere foretold the brief peace that follows here
themes: A governor chosen from among the conquered
Scattered men gathering to one place
Names that reappear later in the story
A brief calm that no prophecy promised

9.pericope_label: Fear not to serve the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and it shall be well with you
debates: Why an oath was needed at all
What the clause about the cities means
Why the settlement did not last
outliers: Calvin holds that the governor risked his own life in receiving men the conquerors would rather not have left in the land
Ellicott dates the whole scene to the autumn from the fruits that are named
themes: An oath required by the state of the times
Power used for the public good rather than for favour
Plenty gathered from fields whose owners were gone
A settlement destroyed from within

13.pericope_label: Dost thou certainly know that Baalis hath sent Ishmael to slay thee? But Gedaliah believed them not
debates: Whether the refusal to believe the warning was greatness of soul or a fault
What the king of the Ammonites hoped to gain
Whether the governor should have acted on the information
outliers: Clarke holds that a little soul is ever suspicious and a great mind the contrary, and makes the credulity a proof of greatness
Calvin answers the question why God allowed so good a man to be killed by saying that death came to him as a mercy before worse things could
themes: A warning given twice and refused twice
Virtue and fault mixed in one act
A medium sought between simplicity and cruelty
A death that undid a settlement
